paragraphs: Friend, here's the heart of it. Tyre hears Jerusalem is in ruins and says, "Aha!" (Ezekiel 26:2). Not a prayer. Not a casserole. An "Aha!" And God answers with "Behold, O Tyre, I am against you…" (Ezekiel 26:3). So watch how you take somebody else's bad day, baker, because God is watching too.

Tyre was a city of renown, powerful on the sea, and the princes of the sea were the ones left trembling over her (Ezekiel 26:16-17). I think that's the thing to sit with. Power, wealth and fancy walls feel like a sure thing until the LORD says otherwise. Nothing you build, earn or stack up can hold if God is against it, and you can't talk your way around that one.

But look at the line God keeps coming back to: "Then they will know that I am the LORD" (Ezekiel 26:6). Everything in this chapter points there, and He says it with "for I, the LORD, have spoken…" (Ezekiel 26:14). So put your weight on the One who doesn't fall, instead of on walls, wins or a bigger parking spot. Hold your neighbor's hard season with a soft heart, baker, and keep your trust where it can't be scraped down to a bare rock.
